item: Encrypted opens are counted per collect pass (file, thread family, CPU) and the custody log is opened once per flush instead of once per stored article
key_paths: src/database/open_stats.py; src/database/connect.py; src/monitoring/collect_perf.py; src/scheduler/runner.py; src/ingest/pipeline.py; src/ingest/batch.py; tests/test_open_stats.py; tests/test_custody_batch.py
summary: Opening an encrypted file derives its key again (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 x 256,000, 163 ms of thread CPU median on one core) and nothing counted the opens. open_stats counts each keyed attempt on an existing encrypted file (failed ones and each page size tried included) by app database file and thread family with the opening thread's CPU, in the pass summary line and the run report as encrypted_opens; numbers and two closed vocabularies only, 32 rows kept and 11 printed with exact totals, an unmeasured CPU absent never zero. _maybe_record_custody opened a CustodyLog (a keyed connection) for every stored article: 94 of the 118 opens of a 96-article pass on two cores (the same pass with custody off used 36-46% less CPU in two runs); _flush_batched now opens one per flush (_CustodyBatch, a with block, dropped after a failed write, reopened when the custody settings or the passphrase change mid-flush, entry read before the log is touched): opens 118 to 32, CPU 51.7 s to 34.3 s at flush size 8 (one run, development machine). The field bundles put custody at about 2 CPU-s a minute, not the 41 one thread showed, so the counter exists to say what the 41 is; C (a per-thread cache) waits for its numbers and a ruling.
